mechanics.name: Come and Get Me!
mechanics.currentEffect: After unhooking a Survivor, while crouched and motionless press the Active Ability button. Injured or Dying Survivors within 24 metres suppress their Grunts of Pain, Pools of Blood and Scratch Marks for 10/12.5/15 seconds. You scream and your Aura is revealed to the Killer for 5 seconds.
activation: Crouch and remain motionless, then use Active Ability.
Ends/deactivates when: Suppression ends after 10/12.5/15 seconds; your Aura reveal ends after 5 seconds.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (9.1.0): Added suppression of Grunts of Pain to the effects on nearby injured or Dying Survivors.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: After an unhook, you can briefly hide nearby injured or downed teammates' trails, at the cost of revealing yourself.
duration: Your Aura revealed to Killer: 5 seconds.
specialInteractions: Affects injured or Dying Survivors within 24 metres; you scream and reveal your Aura to the Killer.

editorial.summary: After unhooking, you can hide nearby injured or downed teammates' pain sounds, Blood, and Scratch Marks for up to 15 seconds, but you scream and reveal your own Aura for 5 seconds.
useCases: Protect the unhooked Survivor's escape trail after a dangerous rescue.
Hide nearby slugged or injured teammates while deliberately drawing Killer attention to yourself.
Use in SWF when the team wants one Survivor to become the obvious decoy.
counters: You reveal yourself to the Killer.
Requires crouching and standing still to activate after an unhook.
Only helps injured or downed teammates within 24 metres.
pros: Creates a deliberate decoy role for the perk owner.
cons: Activation is awkward after a rescue.
Requires nearby teammates to be in exactly the right states.
analysis: Come and Get Me! ranks this position because the effect is powerful but almost aggressively altruistic. After an unhook, the user can erase major tracking cues for nearby injured and downed teammates while explicitly screaming and showing their own Aura to the Killer.

In a coordinated team that can be a real strategy. The rescuer becomes the decoy while the unhooked Survivor and nearby injured teammates disappear from normal tracking, potentially redirecting the Killer away from a vulnerable target.

The same design is dangerous in Solo Q. Revealing yourself without knowing what teammates will do can simply hand the Killer a fresh chase. The crouched, motionless activation also asks for a tiny setup window during an already hectic rescue.
The perk has enough teamplay potential for C, but its risk is not theoretical. You are buying stealth for others with your own visibility.
editorial.verdict: A deliberate decoy perk for coordinated altruism. Come and Get Me! can hide the team beautifully, provided you are happy to paint a target on yourself.
